pages.scan: Read with the Read tool: works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-05.png (page number 5 printed at the bottom). The page has four panels: a wide top tier, a wide middle tier, and a bottom tier split into a left and a right panel. Panel A (top, wide): the first thing I read is the speech balloon at upper right, "Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in." Its tail points down to the placeholder labelled ananya (centre-right). Next I read the teal caption box at lower left, "PATIENT DETAILS: current vitals · prior health info · allergy panel · AI mic option · patient docs · lab reports". The ravi placeholder at far right has no balloon (silent, listening). Panel B (middle, wide): the upper-left balloon "May the AI listen and save notes of our talk?" has its tail to ananya (left). My eye then crossed along the top row to the upper-right balloon "Yes, I agree.", tail to ravi (right). Last I read the teal caption in the lower centre, "AI VOICE CONSENT: asked at the first visit, before any voice is saved". Panel C (bottom left): the upper-left balloon "I've been feeling tired lately." has a long diagonal tail to ravi (right of the panel). Below it is the teal caption at lower left, "SOAP NOTES: fill in manually and choose ICD or SNOMED codes, or let AI listen and summarise the conversation". Ananya is not shown in this panel. Panel D (bottom right): a white-bordered narration box at the top reads "Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human." Below it the ananya placeholder appears in the centre with no balloon (silent reaction or listening). A ravi label dot sits at the lower-right edge with no placeholder rectangle. Speaker order as I read it: Ananya greets and asks her question, Ananya asks for consent, Ravi agrees, Ravi gives his complaint, closing narration.
pages.observation: 1) Panel A: the caption sits at lower LEFT and the balloon at upper RIGHT. A strict left-to-right reader could start with the caption. I read the balloon first because it is clearly higher, but the order is not firmly guided. 2) Possible skipped or delayed reply: Ananya's question "Tell me what brings you in." gets no answer in Panel A. Next she asks a different question, the AI consent, which Ravi answers. Only in Panel C does "I've been feeling tired lately." answer the first question. The consent request interrupts the greeting without any bridging line, so a reader may briefly feel Ravi skipped her question, or that "Yes, I agree." answers "what brings you in". 3) Panel B: the consent caption sits horizontally between the question and the answer but lower down. I read question, then answer, then caption. Another reader could go question, caption, answer. Both orders make sense, but the caption breaks up the exchange visually. 4) Panel C: the tail from "I've been feeling tired lately." is long and runs diagonally across empty space to ravi. It is clear but long. Ananya is absent, so the reader sees no listener reacting to the complaint. 5) Panel D: Ravi has a label dot at the lower-right corner but no placeholder box. It is unclear whether he is meant to be visible, partly out of frame, or missing. Ananya's silent reaction is the only acting in the panel. 6) Left/right placement stays consistent: Ananya is to the left of Ravi in Panels A, B and D, and Ravi is on the right in C. 7) No balloon or caption overlaps any character placeholder. The teal captions take up a large share of Panels A and C (about a third to half of the lower area). They would compete with the figures once art is drawn, especially the Panel C caption, which fills most of the lower-left quadrant. 8) All text was legible. The fixed-width font spaces the letters widely but reads clearly. I found no text I could not read.
